messages:
Alice M.: quick follow-up to the on‑prem/air‑gapped RFC — main ops concern is bundle size and operator UX for upgrades. if customers are on slow links, full OCI images will be painful. ideas?

Ben K.: totally. we should support delta patches where possible. but deltas across quantized weights + different model variants are messy. split runtime vs model artifacts?

Carla R.: +1 on splits. propose 'patch bundles' that are composed of layers: runtime (binaries/config), artifacts (model shards), migrations (db/metadata). each layer signed separately. aim for <200MB for runtime patches where feasible. :memo:

Dan S.: how do we compute deltas reliably when a customer uses custom quantization or a different shard layout? risk of producing bad patch that corrupts model files.

Emily T.: practical path: use bsdiff/xdelta for code/runtime. for models, prefer chunked full-replace with zstd compression + chunk signatures so we can resume and verify. deltas for models are low ROI unless we control all variants.

Alice M.: ops flow sketch: customer downloads bundle(s) to an airgapped medium, then runs: 
```
redwood-upgrade apply --offline /mnt/usb/redwood-patch-202603.tar.zst --verify-only
redwood-upgrade apply --offline /mnt/usb/redwood-patch-202603.tar.zst --apply
```
We need idempotency, resume, and safe rollback paths.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary cluster upgrade 1/10 success: 2026-03-06T14:22Z. logs: checksum OK, migration ran in 32s.

Ben K.: signing model: we need offline signing workflows. support two modes: 1) redwood-signed bundles (our default), 2) customer-signed bundles for private installs. provide tooling to generate signing manifests and verify via KMS/HSM when available.

Carla R.: and include a clear chain-of-trust doc: how to rotate keys, how to validate offline. also add a signed manifest file: `manifest.json.sig` next to `manifest.json`.

Dan S.: for k8s private installs we can ship a lightweight controller that validates bundle signatures, unpacks into a PVC, and then coordinates rolling restart of pods. controller should expose a `ClusterUpgrade` CRD with status and conditions. example: 
```
apiVersion: platform.redwood/v1
kind: ClusterUpgrade
metadata:
  name: offline-2026-03
spec:
  bundleRef: /mnt/usb/redwood-patch-202603.tar.zst
  verifyOnly: false
```

Emily T.: DB migrations: must be backward compatible in a 2-step pattern. first deploy additive changes (columns, flags), then run migration job, then switch traffic. always include migration dry-run output in the bundle. fallback: feature flag that toggles new behavior until next patch.

Alice M.: rollback strategy? if migration runs and fails, we should abort and attempt automatic revert for code changes but db revert is hard. we should require backups and provide `redwood-upgrade rollback --to <bundle-id>` that re-applies previous bundle and runs compensating migrations if available.

Ben K.: add disk-space preflight: fail with clear message if free < X GB. prefer streaming apply that writes chunks directly to final location then fsync per chunk to avoid huge temp usage.

Carla R.: logging and observability: each upgrade run should emit a single JSON trace file in `/var/log/redwood/upgrade/<bundle-id>.trace.json` (signed). includes steps, checksums, durations. helpful for support in airgap cases.

Dan S.: edge-case: partial bundle missing layers. verifier should fail fast and provide remediation: list missing files + expected checksums. also support `--repair` mode that tries to find incremental bundle parts on disk.

Emily T.: QA: we'll do canary on hosted, then dedicated staging, then a private on‑prem customer test with their infra person. automate tests for resume and power-failure simulation.

Alice M.: action items: Ben => delta spec + PoC, Carla => manifest/signing doc + trace format, Dan => k8s controller CRD + prototype, Emily => migration compatibility guide + test plan. I'll fold these into RFC v2 for review next week. :+1:
